notes.title: Option value pipeline: raw argv string to typed callback kwarg
answers: How does --count 3 become an int in the callback?
Where does click do type conversion for options?
Where are envvar and default lookups done and in what precedence?
Where to change option value source precedence?
notes.body:
Flow: Command.main -> make_context -> Command.parse_args (core.py) -> make_parser (each Option.add_to_parser registers dest/action/nargs) -> _OptionParser.parse_args (parser.py) -> _process_args_for_options -> _process_opts -> _match_long_opt/_match_short_opt -> _get_value_from_state (pops raw str) -> _Option.process stores in state.opts. Parser does NO conversion/defaults.
Then parse_args loops iter_params_for_processing(param_order, params) calling Parameter.handle_parse_result -> consume_value -> process_value -> writes ctx.params[name].
- Source precedence in Parameter.consume_value (Option.consume_value wraps it, adds prompt/FLAG_NEEDS_VALUE): commandline opts > value_from_envvar (resolve_envvar_value; Option adds auto_envvar_prefix `{PREFIX}_{NAME.upper()}`) > ctx.lookup_default (default_map) > get_default (Option.get_default resolves default=True to flag_value for non-bool flags; callables are called).
- Conversion: Parameter.process_value -> type_cast_value (handles nargs/multiple, tuples) -> ParamType.__call__ (None passthrough) -> convert (e.g. _NumberParamTypeBase.convert calls _number_class, fail -> BadParameter). Applies to all sources incl. defaults/envvars (envvars split via type.split_envvar_value for nargs!=1/multiple). Then required/value_is_missing check, then param callback.
- Afterwards parse_args turns leftover UNSET into None; Command.invoke -> Context.invoke(self.callback, **ctx.params).
